A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FAF study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including the additional Appendix G in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original FAF evaluations, runtime measurements, ablations, SHAP analyses, GESN comparisons and preliminary GraphLand results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds feature-reduction experiments and preliminary GraphBench evaluations. Appendix G separately identifies reproduced results from prior work.

M1.justification: The core aggregation equations and MLP pipeline remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 introduces an evaluated optional Drop-Span step that removes linearly dependent feature columns; v1 only suggested dimensionality reduction as a possible remedy.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds preliminary evaluations on GraphBench's quotes and replies tasks, measured by MAE. The fourteen main benchmarks and four GraphLand datasets are retained, making this a limited extension of coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 4 evaluates PCA as a feature-reduction comparator alongside Drop-Span and unreduced FAF4. Existing GNN, GESN and GraphLand comparator sets remain unchanged. The GATv2-to-GAT prose edit matches the GAT labels already present in v1's unchanged tables, rather than establishing a baseline replacement.

E3.justification: The added compression experiment compares alternative feature preprocessing and input dimensions. GraphBench introduces test MAE and uses GraphLand-derived hyperparameters without further tuning. Existing experimental splits, hyperparameter grids and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 and Table 4 add an analysis of whether feature reduction preserves prediction performance across five retained datasets, comparing Drop-Span with PCA. Existing reducer, hop, classifier, rewiring, KA and SHAP analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Table 4 introduces performance reporting through point estimates without variability or a stated repeat count, unlike the retained performance comparisons. Existing run/split descriptions and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged; GraphBench uses the existing ± format without specifying its repeat count.

E6.justification: Existing results are unchanged. New Table 4 reports Cora performance of 0.818, 0.8226 and 0.6632 for FAF4, Drop-Span and PCA. Table 17 adds FAF MAEs of 0.661 and 0.579 versus GNN values of 0.768 and 0.694 on quotes and replies. Tables 18–19 reproduce prior-work results.

T1.justification: Theorems 4.1–4.2, the proof and the two-hop example are retained. v2 clarifies multiset notation and that orthogonality concerns distinct feature states, consistent with the existing proof; it adds no substantive mathematical result or revised derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the claim that FAFs compete on twelve of fourteen main benchmarks, with Roman-Empire and Minesweeper as exceptions. The theoretical message and recommendations for stronger tabular baselines and harder benchmarks remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations concerning information discarding versus injectivity and why PCA may obscure sparse predictive signals. Appendix F adds substantive qualifications about incomplete tuning and why preliminary GraphLand results cannot establish that learned aggregation is necessary.

D1.justification: v2 documents the feature-column removal procedure and original/reduced input dimensions, and explains that GraphBench uses transferred GraphLand hyperparameters without retuning. Existing code access, hardware and main training details are retained; the new experiments remain only partly specified.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against close alternatives: SIGN, GAMLP and HOGA, plus a dedicated discussion of graph tabularization for foundation models by Eremeev, Choi and Hayler. It distinguishes FAF's nonlinear reducers and analytical aims from these approaches. Appendix A also expands the comparison with GIN's injectivity argument.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized prose expansions, clarifies terminology, refines appendix headings and adds Appendix G. It also updates the publication footer and reorders acknowledgments and the impact statement. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds feature-reduction Table 4, GraphBench Table 17 and reproduced Tables 18–19. Existing figures and tables are retained, with renumbering and relocation, including Figure 4. Figure 1's caption is expanded; the existing plots are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 turns the suggested feature-reduction remedy into an empirical comparison, adds preliminary benchmark evidence and improves positioning against closely related methods. These strengthen the paper while leaving its central evidence intact. Missing uncertainty in Table 4 and sparse details for the new evaluations limit the strength of these additions, supporting a modest overall improvement.
